description: A struck drum head modelled one vibrating mode at a time, covering tom, timpani, kick, snare, gong, steel pan, frame drum and tabla from one set of controls

params.text: Sets the drum's diameter, 6 to 22 inches, shown in inches and centimetres on the tooltip
Sets the head tension, read as a pitch offset of up to 8.4 semitones either way
Sets the head's bending stiffness, which pushes the modes from a drum head's uneven ratios toward a plate's
Closes the bottom of the shell, from an open shell at one end of the travel to a sealed kettle at the other, which pulls the modes toward a kettledrum's harmonic series
Sets how long the drum rings, 80ms to 7 seconds, scaled by the size as well
Sets how much faster the high modes die away than the low ones
Sets how much the struck head drives the head underneath it
Sets the tuning of the head underneath as a ratio to the struck one
Blends the beater from soft felt to hard stick, shown as a beater name and a contact time on the tooltip
Sets the beater's mass, 10 to 70 grams
Sets how far the pitch drops after the hit, from the head being driven hard
Sets how much of a hand is resting on the head, which subtracts whichever modes are alive at that spot
Sets how much snare wire is under the drum
Sets how tight the wires are, from a loose buzz to a tight snap
Strikes the drum on each press

inputs.text: Sets how hard the drum is struck, 0-10V
Sets the pitch as a volt per octave
Moves the strike point across the head, ±5V added to the strike position
Moves the strike point across the head, ±5V added to the strike position
Changes the diameter, ±5V added to the size knob
Changes the head tension, ±5V added to the tension knob
Changes the head stiffness, ±5V added to the material knob
Changes how far the shell is closed, ±5V added to the air knob
Changes how much of a hand is on the head, ±5V added to the muffle knob
Changes the ring time, ±5V added to the decay knob
Changes how fast the high modes die, ±5V added to the tone knob
Changes the beater hardness, ±5V added to the beater knob

outputs.text: The head and the wires together, at the level knob's setting
The head on its own, without the wires
The snare wires on their own, without the head

notes: the module makes no sound until it is struck, by the HIT button, a rise at the gate jack, or a click on the drawn head
the head is drawn as it actually moves, and clicking or dragging on it both strikes the drum and sets where it is struck; that surface cannot be reached by clicking for help
the diameter and the tension move every mode by the same factor and leave their ratios alone, so acoustically they do the same thing
what separates a small tight drum from a large slack one at the same pitch is the material, the air cavity, and the way the damping follows the size
menu: Head view: Flat, 3D — chooses whether the drawn head is seen face on or in perspective
Instruments — a submenu of presets, each setting the whole panel to one of the eight instruments the model covers
